ruleEliminatedCanReturn.title: Eliminated Can Return
ruleEliminatedCanReturn.help: By default, a player is eliminated when all of their balls are pocketed. If an opponent commits a foul, one of that player's balls can return to the table, allowing them to re-enter the game.

foulPocketOwnBall.title: Pocketing Own Ball
foulPocketOwnBall.help: Occurs when a player pockets their own ball.

breakLayout.title: Break Layout
breakLayout.help: Choose whether the opening rack layout is fixed or randomized.

breakFillers.title: Use Filler Balls On Break
breakFillers.help: When enabled, filler balls are added on the break for player counts that need them.

ruleReturnOpponentBalls.title: Return Opponent Balls On
ruleReturnOpponentBalls.help: Choose which fouls can return an opponent's ball to the table.

field.title: Playing Field
description: Depending on player count, each player is assigned a group of 3 to 7 balls in a given color.
Unlike 8 Ball, your group is the set you must protect. Your goal is to pocket your opponents' balls while keeping at least one of your own on the table.

breaking.title: Starting the game (Breaking)
description: The opening shot starts the match by spreading the rack. Match settings may use a fixed or random break layout, and some player counts can include filler balls (marked with a red cross).
A legal break gives the game a fair start. As in other pool games, scratching the cue ball on break is a foul and usually gives your opponents an advantage.

gameplay.title: Gameplay
description: On your turn, target and pocket balls that belong to other players. Pocketing one of your own balls is a foul.
If all balls from your group are pocketed, you are eliminated. In some rulesets, fouls can return an opponent's ball to the table, which can bring eliminated players back into the game.

objective.title: Objective
description: Be the last player with at least one ball remaining from your group. Everyone else must be eliminated.
Choose your shots carefully: aggressive play can eliminate opponents quickly, but mistakes and fouls can undo your progress.
